attacks_attempted: Enumerated the estate MCP profile tools (positive allowlist of 6; propose/audit_changed structurally unregistered/undispatchable, no alias/default/omitted-profile bypass, no /propose REST route); flag-off inertness (estate paths guarded by estate_read_only_enabled; CLI exit 2 without flag; unsafe-config startup fail-closed); cross-tenant identity drift (wrong iss/aud/multi-aud/sub/azp/actor_type/scopes/org — all 401/403/400); /audit repo_root not caller-selectable (_ensure_within_repo); health over-claim (issuer_pinned bool only); secret sweep (signing-keys public-key-only; no secret in diff); binding-header path-traversal (echo-only, no filesystem sink).
tests_observed: tests/test_service_api.py + tests/scp_mcp: 133 passed, 1 failed (the pre-existing baseline test_no_private_keys_committed on files byte-identical to base, outside this diff). All new estate negatives pass.
summary: The Estate read facade and MCP profile hold all five security invariants. The MCP allowlist is a genuine positive allowlist (propose/audit_changed structurally undispatchable via the estate profile); no REST mutation route exists; unknown/omitted profile selectors resolve to legacy. The feature is off by default and inert when off; enabling with any unsafe config fails startup fail-closed. Auth is enforced end-to-end with exact claim + org-binding matching; cross-tenant/multi-audience/wrong-scope/wrong-issuer denied. Health truthful; no secret leak; /audit cannot target an external root. Findings LOW/NIT only.

findings.summary: status_payload() exposes the full CT_ISSUER value via unauthenticated /status-app/health and /status, whereas health_payload() exposes only issuer_pinned:bool.
findings.disposition: NOT_APPLICABLE - an OIDC issuer is a public identifier (which CT tenant SCP trusts), not a secret; /status is an operational endpoint. Recorded as a tracked consistency hardening (could reduce to issuer_pinned bool) but not a disclosure defect.

findings.summary: Only listing-exclusion of propose/audit_changed was asserted, not call-level rejection through the estate profile.
findings.disposition: FIXED - fix round adds a call-level negative constructing ScpMcpServer(profile='estate-read-only') and invoking propose/audit_changed, asserting ToolError('Unknown tool: ...'); plus an anti-vacuity counterpart proving they ARE reachable under the legacy profile (profile-scoped restriction, not global non-registration).

findings.summary: No test for a fully unauthenticated request (no Authorization header) to an estate REST endpoint returning 401.
findings.disposition: FIXED - fix round adds test_estate_profile_rejects_unauthenticated_request (estate facade enabled, GET /registry with binding headers but no token -> 401).

findings.summary: _ESTATE_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN permits '/' and '.'; and the match relies on the 'scopes' (plural) claim name.
findings.disposition: NOT_APPLICABLE - (a) binding identifiers are echo-only in request_binding and never reach a filesystem sink; active_org_id is compared to the CT-signed claim. (b) Confirmed against the CT contract: control-tower/auth/tokens.py emits the plural `scopes` claim (verified: `payload["scopes"] = scopes`), matching SCP's expectation - so no functional break. Path-separator tightening recorded as a tracked defense-in-depth hardening (no current exploitability).
